Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

Lesson Plan: Introduction to Probability (High-School, 1 × 90-minute block or 2 × 45-minute periods)

-------------------------------------------------
1. Overall Goal
Students will understand and apply foundational probability concepts (sample space, event, theoretical vs. experimental probability, compound events) and will collect, model, and interpret probabilistic data.

2. Standards Alignment (examples, adapt to local curriculum)
• Common Core HS-S-CP.A.1 – Understand independence and conditional probability.
• CCSS HS-S-CP.A.2 – Understand probability of compound events.
• NGSS Practice 4 – Analyzing and interpreting data.
• ISTE 4.b – Use digital tools to analyze data and represent probability models.

3. Learning Objectives (SMART)
By the end of the lesson, students will be able to:
1. Define key vocabulary: outcome, event, sample space, probability, theoretical, experimental.  
2. Calculate theoretical probability for single simple events (dice, coins, spinners) with 80 % accuracy.  
3. Conduct a 30-trial experiment and compute experimental probability; compare it to the theoretical value in writing (≥ 2 sentence explanation).  
4. Use a tree diagram or area model to represent a two-step compound event and compute its probability.

4. Materials & Technology
• One fair coin per pair of students  
• One six-sided die per pair  
• Decks of cards (optional)  
• Chart paper / whiteboard  
• Student handouts: guided notes, exit ticket, tree-diagram template  
• Chromebooks/tablets (optional) with Google Sheets or probability-simulator site  
• Projector/slide deck with visuals

5. Vocabulary
Outcome, Sample Space, Event, Favorable Outcomes, Theoretical Probability, Experimental Probability, Compound Event, Independence.

6. Anticipatory Set (5 min)
Display a weather forecast screenshot (e.g., “30 % chance of rain”). Ask: “What does 30 % mean? Will it rain or not?” Solicit quick thoughts; connect to uncertainty and decision-making.

7. Direct Instruction & Guided Notes (20 min)
• Define sample space; illustrate with coin, die, spinner visuals.  
• Formula: P(event) = (# favorable outcomes)/(# total outcomes).  
• Work through two examples (coin heads; rolling an even on a die) with class solving on mini-whiteboards.  
• Distinguish theoretical vs. experimental probability. Brief anecdote: long-run fairness.

8. Guided Practice Activity 1 – Coin Toss Lab (15 min)
Pairs toss a coin 30 times; tally heads/tails. Students calculate experimental probability and fill class data into a collaborative Google Sheet or chart. Class computes aggregate results and compares to 0.5. Discuss variability and Law of Large Numbers idea (qualitatively).

9. Mini-Lecture: Compound Events (10 min)
• Introduce “AND” probability for independent events: P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B).  
• Build tree diagram for “flip a coin then roll a 3 on a die”. Emphasize branches and multiplying along paths.

10. Guided Practice Activity 2 – Spinner + Coin (15 min)
Provide spinner picture (4 equal colors). Task sheet: a) probability of blue then heads; b) not blue and tails; c) either/or situations. Students complete tree diagram template in pairs; circulate for checks.

11. Independent Practice / Application (10 min)
Worksheet: 5 mixed problems (single-event, experimental vs. theoretical interpretation, draw tree diagram, compute probability of drawing a heart then rolling an even).

12. Closure (5 min)
Return to weather forecast image. Ask: “If forecast shows 80 % chance, how many of the next 10 similar days would we expect to rain?” Students respond on exit slips (include 1 reflection on difference between theoretical & experimental they observed).

13. Assessment
• Formative: whiteboard responses, pair discussions, teacher observation, worksheet checks.  
• Summative: Exit ticket (5 pts) – Q1 theoretical calc, Q2 short answer comparing their coin results to theory.

14. Differentiation / UDL
• Supports: Provide vocabulary cards, color-coded tree branches, use tactile dice.  
• Extensions: Ask advanced students to calculate “at least one head in 3 flips”, introduce complements.  
• ELL: Visuals of sample spaces, sentence frames (“The probability of ___ is ___ because…”).  
• SPED: Pre-fill part of tree diagram, allow calculator.

15. Homework (optional)
Interactive online simulation (e.g., PhET “Plinko Probability”) for 100 trials; screenshot distribution and write a 100-word reflection on convergence to theoretical.

16. Reflection for Teacher (post-class)
• Were misconceptions about fairness addressed?  
• Did group work engage all?  
• Plan next lesson on conditional probability or permutations/combinations based on exit-ticket data.
